neighbours.label: the token ' RFC' in citations of Internet standards, on a dense weak unit that also fires on Russian and Arabic word pieces
fire: Header folding was deprecated by RFC 7230 for HTTP messages.
The JSON text format is specified in RFC 8259 by the IETF.
Email message syntax is defined by RFC 5322 and older drafts.
Our parser accepts dates in the format given by RFC 3339 only.
The keywords MUST and SHOULD are used as in RFC 2119 here.
Base64 encoding follows the alphabet in RFC 4648 section four.
The TLS handshake was revised substantially in RFC 8446.
Cookies are parsed according to the rules of RFC 6265.
quiet: Header folding was deprecated by version 1.1 of the proposal.
The JSON text format is specified in chapter 3 of the manual.
Email message syntax is defined by the old mail software.
Our parser accepts dates in the format given by the user only.
The keywords MUST and SHOULD are written in capital letters here.
Base64 encoding uses an alphabet of sixty-four characters.
The TLS handshake was revised substantially last year.
Cookies are parsed according to the rules of the browser.
